faq.q: How far is Sotogrande from Marbella by boat?
faq.a: Sotogrande is roughly 30 nautical miles south of Marbella. Depending on your boat's cruising speed (18–28 knots for our fleet), the journey takes 60–90 minutes. We depart from Puerto Banús, so you'll enjoy the Costa del Sol coastline along the way.

faq.q: Can I moor at Sotogrande Marina during the polo final?
faq.a: Yes, Sotogrande Marina has visitor berths, but they fill up quickly during the polo final. We recommend pre-booking your mooring or anchoring nearby (e.g., Cala del Faro) and taking a short tender ride ashore. Your skipper can advise on the best option.

faq.q: What is included in the boat rental price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. For longer charters, you can add catering or water toys.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a group of 10 going to the polo final?
faq.a: The Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Astondoa 40 (9 pax) are excellent for smaller groups, both from €749/2h. For up to 12 pax with more space and a jet ski, go for the Mangusta 80 (from €4,719/4h). All depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: Can I watch the polo final from the boat?
faq.a: You can anchor off Santa María Polo Club's beach or near the Sotogrande coast for a distant view, but the final itself is best enjoyed from the club's stands. Most guests moor at Sotogrande Marina and walk 15 minutes to the club.

faq.q: What is the best time to depart Marbella for the polo final?
faq.a: The final typically starts mid-afternoon. We suggest departing Puerto Banús between 10:00 and 11:00 to cruise leisurely, anchor for lunch, and arrive at Sotogrande by 13:00–14:00. Return after the final around 18:00–19:00.

faq.q: Are there any extra costs for fuel or skipper?
faq.a: No. Fuel, skipper, drinks, snacks, and insurance are all included in the price shown. The only optional extras are premium catering, water toys (jet ski, paddleboard), or extended hours beyond the booked time.

faq.q: How do I book a boat for the Sotogrande Polo Final 2037?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp (button on our site) or use the booking form. Mention 'Sotogrande Polo Final 2037' to confirm availability. We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks in advance, especially for larger yachts like the Mangusta 80.

data.body_html:
The Sotogrande Polo Final 2037 is the highlight of the summer season on the Costa del Sol. Held at the legendary Santa María Polo Club, this prestigious event draws international crowds. But why queue for a taxi when you can arrive in style? Renting a boat from Marbella transforms the day into a full Mediterranean experience: cruise south along the coast, drop anchor for a swim, enjoy lunch on deck, and then step ashore just minutes from the final. This guide covers everything you need to know — from which boat to book to what's included — for the ultimate polo day.

Why Rent a Boat for the Sotogrande Polo Final 2037?

Driving from Marbella to Sotogrande takes about 45 minutes, but you'll sit in traffic and pay for parking. A boat charter turns the journey into the main event. Depart from Puerto Banús, cruise past the Golden Mile, Estepona, and the Rock of Gibraltar on the horizon. The sea breeze keeps you cool, and you can swim at empty coves like Cala del Faro before the match. After the final, you're back on board for a sunset sail — no queues, no hassle. Plus, with a skipper included, everyone can enjoy the champagne.

Our Fleet for the Sotogrande Polo Final 2037

We operate from Puerto Banús and offer a range of boats suitable for groups of 5 to 12. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava), light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%). No surprises.

Astondoa 40 & Azimut 39

Perfect for smaller groups (9–11 pax). These 12.5m motor yachts are fast (25+ knots) and well-equipped. Price: €749/2h or €2,299/8h — ideal for a full-day outing to the polo final.

Mangusta 80 (24m)

For those who want space, speed, and a free jet ski. The Mangusta 80 (and its grey variant) accommodates 12 pax. Minimum charter: 4 hours at €4,719. Includes a jet ski to play with during the cruise.

Other Options

We also have the Azimut 58 Flybridge, Ferretti 94, Canados 86, and more — all departing Puerto Banús. For pricing, contact us via WhatsApp. See the full fleet list for details.

Sample Itinerary: Marbella to Sotogrande

  • 10:00 — Board your boat at Puerto Banús. Meet skipper, safety briefing.
  • 10:30 — Depart. Cruise south past Cabopino, Calahonda, and Estepona.
  • 11:30 — Anchor at Cala del Faro or Playa de Torreguadiaro for a swim and light lunch.
  • 13:00 — Arrive Sotogrande Marina or anchor off Santa María Polo Club beach.
  • 14:00–18:00 — Enjoy the polo final. Tender to shore if anchored.
  • 18:30 — Depart Sotogrande. Sunset cruise back to Marbella.
  • 20:00 — Dock at Puerto Banús. Optional dinner at a beach club.

This itinerary works perfectly with an 8-hour charter (€2,299 for Astondoa 40). Adjust times to suit the final's schedule.

Best Spots to Anchor Near Sotogrande

If you prefer to stay on the water rather than moor at the marina, these anchorages are within 10 minutes of Santa María Polo Club:

  • Cala del Faro — Sheltered cove with clear water, 5 NM north of Sotogrande.
  • Playa de Torreguadiaro — Sandy beach with calm conditions, popular with boaters.
  • Guadiaro River Mouth — Shallow but scenic; good for paddleboarding.
  • Sotogrande Marina — Book a visitor berth in advance for easy access to the club.

What to Expect at the Sotogrande Polo Final 2037

The Santa María Polo Club hosts the final of the summer season in late August. Expect world-class polo, champagne tents, and a sophisticated crowd. Dress code is smart casual — think linen suits, sundresses, and espadrilles. The club has restaurants and bars, but many guests prefer to picnic on their boat. If you want catering, we can arrange a gourmet hamper (contact us for details).
